reason: Clean Water Act section 23 is a cohesive evidentiary provision for analyst certificates, including admissibility and proof, cross-examination with leave, and notice before production.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Analyst certificate evidence, cross-examination, and notice
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections work together on how analyst certificates are used in prosecutions and what procedural protections apply to the opposing party.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an analyst certificate is admissible and proof in Clean Water Act prosecutions, and how cross-examination and notice requirements apply.

reason: Clean Water Act section 24 is a focused service provision identifying sufficient service methods for orders, notices, and other documents and deeming registered-mail service after five days.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service methods and registered-mail deeming rule
proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections specify acceptable service methods and when service by prepaid registered mail is deemed effective.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Clean Water Act orders, notices, and other documents may be served and when registered-mail service is deemed effective.

reason: Clean Water Act section 25 is a cohesive offence and fine provision covering offences, fine ranges, daily multiplication for continuing violations, and the Pesticides Control Act charging rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Clean Water Act offence liability, fine ranges, daily fines, and pesticide charges
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify what conduct is an offence, the fine ranges for individuals and others, the multiplier for continuing violations, and the charging rule for overlapping Pesticides Control Act offences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Clean Water Act offence, fine, continuing-violation, and Pesticides Control Act charging rules.

reason: Clean Water Act section 26 is a cohesive enhanced-fine provision for offences committed for financial advantage or to avoid compliance costs, with a prosecutor notice prerequisite.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Enhanced fines for financial advantage or avoided compliance costs
proposedGroups.reason: The two subsections work together by authorizing fines beyond ordinary maxima in specified financial-benefit circumstances and requiring advance prosecutor notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a judge may impose an enhanced Clean Water Act fine for financial advantage or avoided compliance costs and what notice must be given.

reason: Section 27 is a single offence-classification rule making every non-individual who commits an offence under the Act or regulations subject to absolute liability.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Absolute liability for non-individual Clean Water Act offenders

evidenceText: Every person other than an individual who commits an offence under this Act or the regulations commits an absolute liability offence

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one rule about the liability classification for non-individual offenders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a non-individual who commits a Clean Water Act offence commits an absolute liability offence.

reason: Section 28 is a single limitation-period rule for proceedings in respect of offences under the Act or regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Two-year limitation period for Clean Water Act offence proceedings

evidenceText: Proceedings with respect to an offence under this Act or the regulations may be instituted at any time within two years

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one time limit measured from when the subject matter of the proceedings arose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the two-year period for instituting Clean Water Act or regulation offence proceedings.

reason: Section 29 is a single remedial rule allowing contraventions of the Act, regulations, or specified Minister or Lieutenant-Governor in Council instruments to be restrained in an action by the Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister action to restrain Clean Water Act contraventions

evidenceText: that is contravened may, in addition to any other remedy and to any penalty imposed by law, be restrained in an action at the instance of the Minister

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies the contraventions that can be restrained and confirms the remedy is additional to other remedies and penalties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may bring an action to restrain Clean Water Act contraventions.

reason: Section 30 is a single civil-remedy preservation rule, but the target text includes an apparent stray heading after the operative sentence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Civil remedies unaffected by Clean Water Act offences

evidenceText: No civil remedy for an act or omission is suspended or affected by reason that the act or omission is an offence under this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The operative sentence preserves civil remedies despite offence status; the trailing heading text should not be authored as part of the rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a civil remedy is not suspended or affected because an act or omission is also a Clean Water Act offence.

reason: Section 31 is a cohesive establishment and governance provision for the Land and Water Advisory Committee, including definition, membership, officers, quorum, procedure, and tenure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land and Water Advisory Committee establishment and governance
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections define the Committee and set how it is established, who is appointed, officer designations, quorum, procedural rules, and service at pleasure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Land and Water Advisory Committee is defined, established, appointed, chaired, quorate, procedurally governed, and held at pleasure.

reason: Section 32 covers both the Land and Water Advisory Committee's substantive duties and its supporting powers for submissions, expenses, special-knowledge services, and annual reporting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land and Water Advisory Committee department definition and duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 32(1) and 32(2) define department for the section and list the Committee's duties relating to land and water use information, recommendations, conflict resolution, Act review, Minister requests, and regulated duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definition of department and the Land and Water Advisory Committee's duties concerning land and water use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Committee submissions, expenses, special knowledge, and annual report
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 32(3) through 32(6) provide supporting powers and duties for receiving submissions, paying expenses, engaging special knowledge, submitting an annual report, and legislative tabling.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Committee's powers and duties for submissions, expenses, expert services, annual reporting, and tabling.

reason: Section 33 is a single administration and delegation rule making the Minister responsible for the Act and allowing designation of persons to act on the Minister's behalf.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister administration and designation to act on behalf

evidenceText: The Minister is responsible for the administration of this Act and may designate persons to act on the Minister’s behalf

proposedGroups.reason: The target contains one rule about Ministerial responsibility and designation of persons to act for the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the Minister administers the Clean Water Act and may designate persons to act on the Minister's behalf.

reason: Section 34 is a focused agreement-making power for the Minister, with Lieutenant-Governor in Council approval, to enter agreements that carry out the Act's intent and support committees, consultation, and advice on policies and programs.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister agreements to carry out Clean Water Act objectives
proposedGroups.reason: The provision identifies possible agreement parties and the agreement purposes related to implementing programs, continuing consultation, and advice on Act objectives.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall with whom the Minister may enter agreements under section 34 and what those agreements may establish to carry out the Act's intent.

reason: Section 35 is a single administrative power for the Minister to issue, transfer, suspend, cancel, renew, or reinstate required registrations, licences, permits, and approvals in accordance with regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister powers over Clean Water Act authorizations

evidenceText: Where a registration, licence, permit or approval is required
may issue, transfer, suspend, cancel, renew or reinstate
in accordance with the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: The target is one rule about Minister powers over required authorization instruments and the regulations governing those powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Minister may do with required Clean Water Act registrations, licences, permits, and approvals.

reason: Section 36 is a single register-maintenance duty for authorization applications under the Act or regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Register for Clean Water Act authorization applications

evidenceText: shall maintain a register
with respect to each application for a registration, licence, permit or approval
such information as the Minister considers appropriate

proposedGroups.reason: The target requires the Minister to maintain a register in a suitable form with information about each authorization application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what register the Minister must maintain for Clean Water Act authorization applications.

reason: Section 37 is a single inspection-access rule for the register kept under section 36, including place, time, who may inspect, and fee condition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspection of Clean Water Act authorization register

evidenceText: The register kept under section 36 shall be open for inspection
at the Minister’s office during normal business hours
by any person on payment of the fee

proposedGroups.reason: The target states where and when the register may be inspected and the fee condition for any person inspecting it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when, where, and on what fee condition the section 36 register is open for inspection.

reason: Section 38 is a single payment duty for applicants, persons taking proceedings, authorization holders, and persons using or diverting water to pay regulation-established fees, rentals, and charges in the regulation-established manner.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fees, rentals, and charges for authorizations, proceedings, and water use

evidenceText: An applicant, a person who takes any proceedings
a holder of a registration, licence, permit or approval
a person who uses or diverts water
shall pay the fees, rentals and charges established by regulation

proposedGroups.reason: The provision identifies who must pay and ties the amounts and manner of payment to regulation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must pay Clean Water Act fees, rentals, and charges established by regulation and how payment is established.

reason: Section 39 is a single appeal right for specified authorization suspensions, cancellations, and refusals under the Clean Water Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appeals from Clean Water Act authorization decisions

evidenceText: registration, licence, permit or approval has been suspended or cancelled
application for a registration, licence, permit or approval or for the transfer, renewal or reinstatement
may appeal the suspension, cancellation or refusal

proposedGroups.reason: The target identifies the authorization decisions that may be appealed and ties the appeal to the regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which Clean Water Act authorization suspensions, cancellations, and refusals may be appealed.

reason: Clean Water Act section 40 contains many current regulation-making powers even though the supplied content flags mark the target as repeal-only; the operative text supports authoring, but the flag conflict warrants caution.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for waste, releases, water use, appeals, costs, and measurement

evidenceText: prescribing agricultural activities
prescribing any matter to be waste
respecting the release, handling, disposal or removal
withdrawal, use, storage and handling of water
providing for the appeal
payment and recovery of any costs
methods, standards or tests

proposedGroups.reason: The opening active paragraphs authorize regulations for alteration-related agricultural activities, waste, contaminant releases and handling, water withdrawal and use, appeals, cost recovery, claims, cost collection, and contaminant or waste measurement in water.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Clean Water Act regulation powers for waste, releases, water use, appeals, costs, claims, and contaminant or waste measurement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for water classification and review panels

evidenceText: respecting the establishment of a water classification system
classifying all or any portion of the water of a watercourse
criteria or standards that a class of water is to meet
prohibiting any activity that might impair the quality or quantity
establishing or requiring the Minister to establish a review panel

proposedGroups.reason: The water-classification paragraphs authorize regulations for establishing classification systems, classifying or excluding watercourses, Minister discretion, criteria and standards, activity prohibitions, procedures, conditions, restrictions, and review panels.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for classifying watercourses, setting class standards, restricting impairing activities, and using review panels.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for insurance, potable-water recommendations, and protected areas

evidenceText: respecting insurance coverage or the posting of security
matters in relation to which the Potable Water Advisory Committee makes recommendations
respecting the designation of all or any portion of a watershed, aquifer or ground water recharge area as a protected area

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs authorize regulations for insurance or security conditions, Potable Water Advisory Committee recommendation matters, and protected-area designation and controls to protect water quality or quantity.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for insurance or security, Potable Water Advisory Committee recommendation matters, and protected-area designation and controls.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for contaminant sources, diversions, ice structures, flood hazards, and wells

evidenceText: location, construction, testing, alteration, modification, use, operation, repairing, monitoring, inspection, discharge or removal of sources of contaminant
river diversions, drainage diversions or alterations
structures of any kind on the ice
flood hazard area
establishing an advisory board
location, spacing, construction, testing, alteration, reconditioning, repairing, sealing, capping and abandoning of wells

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs authorize regulations for contaminant sources, dangers of pollution, waterworks, hydro-electric projects, control dams, diversions and alterations, structures on ice or crossing watercourses and wetlands, flood hazard areas, well advisory boards, and well construction or abandonment standards.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for contaminant sources, waterworks, diversions, ice structures, flood hazards, and well construction or abandonment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for notices, Committee duties, authorizations, exemptions, fees, and forms

evidenceText: content of, timing of, publishing of, service of or any other matter relating to any notice, order or other document
establishing the duties of the Land and Water Advisory Committee
issue, transfer, suspension, cancellation, renewal and reinstatement
exemption of persons or classes of persons
establishing fees, rentals and charges
respecting forms

proposedGroups.reason: These paragraphs authorize regulations for notices and documents, Land and Water Advisory Committee duties, authorization processes, permit exemptions and waivers, terms and conditions, fees, rentals, charges, and forms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for notices, Committee duties, authorizations, permit exemptions or waivers, conditions, fees, rentals, charges, and forms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation powers for inspectors, records, confidentiality, and public water supply systems

evidenceText: duties and powers of inspectors and analysts
records to be kept, the returns to be made and the information to be given
confidentiality of documents and other information
defining public water supply system

proposedGroups.reason: The closing active paragraphs authorize regulations for inspector and analyst duties, samples and analysis, records, returns, information, confidentiality, and defining public water supply system.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers for inspectors and analysts, records and returns, confidentiality, and the definition of public water supply system.
